subject: memcg stats flushing (WAS "Re: [PATCH] fuse: disable default bdi strictlimiting")

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that the patch may cause OOM kills due to stale stats in the zswap limits calculation, which uses ratelimited flushing, and suggested adding Song's patch to address this issue.

Reviewer suggested treating cachestat() syscall similarly to memory.stat by performing a full flush on user-space read, unless the syscall is invoked frequently.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed questioned the practicality of a specific concern about incorrect activations leading to thrashing, without providing further details or suggestions.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed noted that the ratelimited flush in vmscan is causing OOM kills during memory pressure tests and suggested investigating this further.

Reviewer suggested that memcg could use batching to update its per-memcg atomic global counter, eliminating the need for flushing and reducing overhead.
reviews.raw_body:
There is also the zswap limits calculation, which Song sent a patch to
change to using ratelimited flushing. I think that case is more
problematic as it can cause OOM kills if we use stale stats (e.g.
after a burst of writeback frees up space in zswap). Adding Song here.

The shrinker case is more benign.

---

I am not sure how the cachestat() syscall is used, but my preference
would be to treat it like memory.stat and do a full flush on userspace
read, unless it's a syscall that is invoked frequently for some
reason.

---

Incorrect activations can lead to thrashing in some cases, but I am
not sure how practical the concern is.

---

We do have an internal test that runs a VM under memory pressure and
we started observing OOM kills after the ratelimited flush was added
in vmscan, so I think it's more problematic than just reclaiming hot
memory, but I didn't look too closely.

---

Also zswap limits calculation. I am not sure how benign the workingset
case is, but it has been ratelimited for a while now AFAICT, so maybe
it's fine.

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch addresses the issue of stale memory cgroup (memcg) stats causing premature OOM kills by proposing a solution to reduce the overhead of updating and flushing these statistics. The idea is for memcg to accumulate updates on a per-CPU basis, then propagate them up to a global atomic counter when it reaches a certain threshold, eliminating the need for frequent flushing. This approach aims to scale better for large machines with many cores and focuses on reducing the number of stats that require flushing, specifically NR_FILE_DIRTY and NR_WRITEBACK in the writeback case.
